This weekend SNL is handing its Halloween show to a woman who used to walk dogs and stream video games on Twitch to pay her bills, and the movie that got her there cost less than a typical house in Los Angeles and went on to make half a billion dollars.

Her name is Inde Navarrette. The movie is Obsession, made by Curry Barker, a 26-year-old former barista from Alabama who did sketch comedy on YouTube. He wrote and directed it himself, and the entire budget was $750,000. Inde plays Nikki, a woman who gets cursed by a wish into loving a guy so hard it turns violent.

Here's why Hollywood lost its mind over it. Horror movies make most of their money opening weekend, because the fans show up right away and then ticket sales drop hard. Obsession opened to $17.2 million, which already beat the $10 million everybody predicted, and then the second weekend it made more money than the first. It went up 39%. The Comscore analyst who's been tracking box office for 33 years said he had nothing to compare it to.

By the time it left US theaters in August, it had $263 million here and $501 million worldwide.

That works out to about $668 back for every dollar it cost to make. Ridley Scott spent $130 million making Prometheus, and this little movie passed that film's entire box office total in 53 days.

Inde had been grinding for years before any of this. She had recurring parts on 13 Reasons Why and Superman & Lois, and most people still couldn't have told you her name. Since Obsession, Marvel cast her as Rogue in the new X-Men, and Apple signed her to lead a thriller from Brad Pitt's company with her name on it as executive producer. One of her SNL promos even jokes about it, with a cast member reminding her they booked her for Halloween because she was in the biggest horror movie of the year.

Zoom out and you see this keeps happening. Kane Parsons was 20 when his Backrooms movie, which started as a YouTube series, made $360 million on about $10 million. Barker is now directing the next Texas Chainsaw Massacre. And the week after Inde hosts, SNL gives the show to Druski, the first online content creator they've ever had host.

The reason comes down to how these guys learned the job. On YouTube you put something out every few weeks, and within hours the comments tell you whether it landed. By the time Barker got a real budget, he'd spent years running free tests on what makes people laugh and scream. A studio that puts $150 million into one sequel gets to find out if it worked once, on opening weekend.

Inde told Variety she feels like she snuck into SNL, which is a pretty funny thing to say when the movie that got you in the door made half a billion dollars.

Breaking Bad, Kick Buttowski and Final Fantasy VII Star Matt Jones Turns 45! 🎙️🎮

Jones may be instantly recognizable as Badger from Breaking Bad, but his unmistakable raspy delivery has also found a home across games and animation. He brings Wedge to life in Final Fantasy VII Remake and Rebirth, voices Pig in Pig Goat Banana Cricket, Gunther Magnuson in Kick Buttowski, and Dave Grant-Gomez in Hamster & Gretel.
